summary: On 29 March 2024 Andres Freund reported a backdoor in the xz compression library's upstream tarballs 5.6.0 and 5.6.1, found after he noticed slow SSH logins and valgrind errors on Debian sid. It was CVE-2024-3094.

overview.background: xz-utils provides the liblzma library. OpenSSH does not link it directly, but Debian and other distributions patch OpenSSH to use libsystemd, which depends on liblzma.
systems: sshd on systems that link it through libsystemd
Debian sid and other pre-release distribution builds
overview.impact: A backdoor that could allow some form of remote access was caught before it reached widely deployed stable releases.
overview.severity: Critical (CVE-2024-3094). Few systems had it, per the report.
overview.gaps: Freund's post says he had not yet analysed exactly what the injected code checks for.

diagrams.title: A backdoor in the build chain reaches sshd
diagrams.caption: Per the report, an obfuscated script in the release tarball modifies the liblzma build, replaces ifunc resolvers and redirects RSA_public_decrypt in sshd.

timeline.e: Malicious test files and build changes are committed upstream.
Freund notices SSH logins using a lot of CPU and valgrind errors.
He uses perf and gdb to trace where execution diverges.
He posts the analysis to oss-security after a preliminary report to the Debian security team.
Distributions revert or pin versions. Red Hat assigns CVE-2024-3094.
Affected pre-release systems are downgraded and rebuilt.

rootCause.trigger: Malicious code was added to xz upstream over several weeks.
rootCause.underlying: The release tarballs included an obfuscated script that was not in the repository's normal source, and test files held the payload.
contributing: Release artifacts not compared to the repository
sshd indirectly linking liblzma via libsystemd

diagnose.step: Measure unexpected CPU use in a daemon.
diagnose.why: Slow SSH logins were the clue.

diagnose.step: Compare behaviour using perf and valgrind.
Compare release tarballs with repository source.

correct.step: Downgrade xz to a version before 5.6.0.
Rebuild systems that built the bad version.
Rotate credentials if exposure is possible.

verify.step: Check sshd loads no unexpected libraries.

prevent.step: Reduce libraries linked into network daemons.

fix.safety: Do not run the exploit or test on production hosts. Use isolated systems.

troubleshoot.scenario: SSH logins on your build host take 0.8 s instead of 0.3 s and valgrind reports errors. You use a rolling distribution.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do?
troubleshoot.answer: Profile sshd, compare libraries and versions, check upstream, pin or downgrade xz and report to your distribution security team.

remediation.answer: List libraries loaded by network daemons.
Verify tarball hash and signature against source.

design.prompt: Design supply-chain defence for a distribution.
design.answer: Reproducible builds, review of build scripts, binary analysis, canary builds and maintainer support.
